purpose: Source-linked review of existing reference rules and safety disposition. Software decisions and synthetic tests are not clinical validation.
scope: No new symptom options, condition IDs, anatomy models, treatment prescriptions or remote medical inference.

entries.type: Conservative application output policy

sources.title: SANJO guideline: diagnostic approach, recommendations 1 and 3
sources.use: A clinical presentation alone cannot confirm or exclude joint infection; suspected infection requires timely assessment.

sources.title: MSD Professional: Splenic Injury
sources.use: Trauma assessment requires attention to potentially serious causes; a superficial reference match cannot establish stability.

sources.title: NHS: chest pain
sources.use: The action for high-risk chest symptoms must not be reduced by a benign-looking reference match.

sources.title: NHS: blood in urine
sources.use: Blood in urine warrants prompt assessment; associated fever changes the immediate evaluation context without proving obstruction.

sources.title: NHS: ectopic pregnancy symptoms
sources.use: Actual pain, shoulder-tip pain or fainting with possible pregnancy changes urgency. Pregnancy possibility alone does not establish pain.

sources.title: MSD Professional: Jaundice
sources.use: Fever and abdominal symptoms are important associated findings; laboratory tests and imaging are needed to distinguish causes.

entries.decision: Separate immediate, same-day and prompt assessment guidance from rule-match scores. When a priority warning is triggered, retained reference cards use the most urgent actual guidance instead of their routine self-care instructions. Priority cards do not display a numerical rank.
entries.appliesTo: Only inputs that already trigger an explicit priority rule. The ordinary no-warning path is unchanged. Coexisting warnings remain visible and are ordered by disposition.
notEstablished: The sources do not validate this application's scores or diagnostic accuracy.
A missing checkbox is unknown, not a negative examination.
A prompt or same-day recommendation is not silently promoted to an emergency recommendation.

positiveExamples.expected: Immediate assessment remains the action on every retained card, including an abdominal-wall reference match.
The bowel-reference score cannot override the same-day assessment instruction.
Immediate guidance precedes prompt guidance; neither warning is discarded.

negativeExamples.expected: No new priority warning; the existing ordinary reference advice is retained.
Prompt assessment remains prompt, not an automatic emergency disposition.
Timing and location alone do not establish abdominal pain.
A risk-context checkbox alone does not invent pain or a condition card.

entries.type: Professional-source review with conservative software mapping
entries.decision: Swelling/redness and local heat or purulent drainage around an existing joint region receive same-day assessment even if fever is unreported. This does not confirm joint infection or gout.

Patella.r: 局部肿胀 + 局部压痛 + 流脓, without reported heat or fever
negativeExamples: Patella.r: 局部肿胀 only; 发热 only
notEstablished: No clinical diagnostic validation, no inferred negative examination, and no new options or condition IDs.

sources.title: AHA/ACC Chest Pain Guideline: pressure/tightness terminology

entries.decision: The existing exertional chest-pressure label counts as chest discomfort for triage. Related radiation labels are recognized as reported pain where their displayed text explicitly says pain, without adding an independent evidence family or diagnosing a cardiac condition. A final audit checked every visible bilingual label rather than IDs alone: the delayed-exercise label already reports soreness; meal-related abdominal pain and twisting/stretching pain already report pain. These observations can satisfy existing triage pain semantics without another generic-pain checkbox, but their evidence families and condition gates are not expanded. Shoulder-tip, flank and groin-radiating pain are still not relabeled upper-abdominal pain.
positiveExamples: Heart: 运动诱发胸闷 + 冷汗
Sternum: 运动诱发胸闷 + 气短
Sternum: 局部压痛 + 活动诱发 + 气短
Rectus femoris: 新运动后1至3天 + 尿色深 + 肌力下降
Actual RUQ: 油腻餐后痛 or 进食后腹痛 + 发热
Sternum: 新运动后1至3天 + 气短
negativeExamples: Heart: 运动诱发胸闷 alone does not produce a cardiac diagnosis card
Timing alone does not establish pain
Sternum: 局部压痛 + 活动诱发 remains non-emergency
Shoulder-tip or flank pain is not relabeled as local upper abdominal pain solely from a model location
Delayed exercise soreness without the dark-urine/strength-or-progression combination is not automatically an emergency.
notEstablished: Neither cardiac disease nor a specific organ lesion is confirmed.

entries.type: Faithful input description and conservative reference display

sources.title: ICHD-3: migraine without aura diagnostic criteria, pages 18–19

entries.decision: Descriptions separate possible patterns from uncollected starting point, actual pain location, laterality, aura, bone tenderness or increased load. Explicit seconds-to-minutes episodes with migraine-like features are shown as a broad headache direction, not a typical migraine reference; the existing English duration label now matches Chinese. Canonical input ordering stabilizes evidence rendering. The same explicit seconds-to-minutes conflict also withholds the typical tension-type reference, preserving a broad direction and all danger actions. The existing urine option English now matches its Chinese wording (unable to pass urine); neither the ID nor its rule is expanded. Actual visible wording is authoritative: the first-step option already reports heel pain, so that location is retained; the particular heel tissue remains unconfirmed.
positiveExamples: Frontal bone: 跳痛 + 畏光 + 短暂发作 returns broad headache direction
Equivalent reordered canonical reports return identical output.
Frontal bone: 紧箍感 + 双侧头痛 + 短暂发作 returns a broad direction, without clinical exclusion.
negativeExamples: Frontal bone: 跳痛 + 畏光 without reported brief episodes retains a qualified migraine-like reference.
notEstablished: This is a conservative display constraint, not medical exclusion of migraine: age, treatment, episode count and full course are missing. No diagnosis is established by a reference match.

sources.use: Terms 02.1542–1547 distinguish interspinales and intertransversarii; 02.1108/02.1110 distinguish the two ligament families. PDF pages 118 and 93.

sources.title: IFAA/FIPAT TA98: muscles of back
sources.use: A04.3.01.014–016 distinguish lateral lumbar intertransversarii dorsal and ventral parts.

entries.decision: Correct the ventral lateral lumbar intertransversarii Chinese name, normalize its dorsal counterpart, and correct intertransverse ligaments. A narrow spine alias retains the existing region after removing the erroneous spinous word.
positiveExamples: Ventral/dorsal parts on both sides use 腰横突间外侧肌 + subdivision.
Intertransverse ligaments use 横突间韧带 on both sides.
negativeExamples: Interspinales remain 棘间肌; interspinous ligaments remain 棘间韧带.
Original English labels, mesh names, side suffixes and clinical regions remain unchanged.
notEstablished: This verifies naming and identity mapping, not geometric laterality or patient pathology.

entries.type: Input-faithful reference copy and single-observation broad assessment

sources.title: Existing bilingual observations and reference content at reviewed project baseline
sources.use: Software source for the actual reported label meanings; this is not independent clinical evidence.

entries.decision: Descriptions present associated cramps, groin radiation, heat, bruising and swelling as possible reference features, not additional patient observations. The existing delayed-exercise timing label explicitly reports soreness, so it supports a single broad basic card; it still counts as one exercise evidence family and cannot alone create a specific condition card.
positiveExamples: Diarrhoea + fever does not report cramps.
Colic + haematuria does not report groin radiation.
Redness + movement restriction does not report local heat.
Pain + injury does not report bruising.
The sole 新运动后1至3天 label already contains soreness in both visible languages.
negativeExamples: Pure durations or worsening without a reported symptom still do not fabricate pain.
Reference gates, why observations and triage are not broadened by the copy changes.
notEstablished: No new clinical association or diagnostic criterion is introduced; this is fidelity to existing inputs and general reference wording.

entries.type: Existing observation semantics, region filtering and conservative source clarification

sources.title: AAE: Tooth pain, sharp pain when biting
sources.use: Biting pain can have several dental causes and warrants dental examination; it does not establish one diagnosis.

sources.title: NIDCR: Temporomandibular disorders
sources.use: Chewing/jaw symptoms can involve the face or neck and require examination; retain head/neck referral contexts.

sources.title: NHS: Temporomandibular disorder
sources.use: Jaw, ear and temple symptoms can be related to chewing.

sources.title: NHS: Toothache
sources.use: Dental review is advised for tooth pain with fever or pain on biting; this page does not establish a mandatory same-day two-checkbox rule.

sources.title: NHS: Dental abscess
sources.use: Suspected abscess needs urgent dental care; current inputs do not prove an abscess.

entries.decision: The existing pain-on-biting observation stays in the pain evidence family but is removed from generic local-pain gates. Existing explicit dental/jaw rules remain. Its visible entries are teeth, jaw, ear, head and neck, including the organ-filter boundary. Old wrong-area inputs remain in the report and receive source-clarification wording rather than being silently erased or converted to limb/abdominal pain. Other independent symptoms and actions remain in force.
positiveExamples: Tooth: 咬合痛 + 牙龋洞 / 外伤后 / 牙龈肿胀 retains the corresponding existing gated reference.
Jaw: 咬合痛 + 张口弹响 retains the existing jaw reference.
Humerus: 咬合痛 + 疼痛 + 外伤后 still has actual local pain and injury evidence; biting does not appear as local evidence.
Ear/head/neck and legacy wrong-area biting with fever/chills receive source-neutral same-day dental/medical assessment.
negativeExamples: 咬合痛 + 疼痛 are not two independent pain observations.
Biting plus injury or posture does not establish arm, knee, abdominal, splenic or local neck pain.
Biting alone is not automatically urgent or a diagnosis.
A separate back-radiation pain label, breathing difficulty or sudden neurological/hearing change keeps its existing action.
notEstablished: Same-day timing for reported biting pain with fever/chills is a conservative application disposition extending the existing dental tier while the source is unconfirmed, not a guideline-validated score or proof of infection.
Anatomy selection cannot confirm the source or side of referred pain. No global symptom or condition ID is added.

entries.type: Conservative dental contact timing for existing reported observations

sources.title: SDCEP: Acute periodontal conditions
sources.use: Pain and gingival swelling can occur in acute periodontal problems. Urgent dental care is distinct from medical emergency care for airway compromise.

sources.title: SDCEP: Timescales for treatment
sources.use: Urgent dental care is the next available clinic, within 24 hours or as soon as practicable, with clinical judgement and local service constraints.

entries.decision: In existing tooth/jaw entries, reported gum swelling with 疼痛, 咬合痛, 持续冷热痛, 自发痛 or 夜间痛 prompts contact with a dentist today for triage and examination. This is a conservative application mapping for unassessed painful swelling, independent of candidate condition names. Injury is neither required nor proof of infection. Existing emergency airway/opening actions remain higher priority.
positiveExamples: Lower canine.l and Mandible: each of the five explicit pain labels plus 牙龈肿胀; no redundant generic pain is needed.
Superficial part of masseter.r consumes the same existing jaw observations; the test checks both deployed detail levels for the actual mesh.
Adding 外伤后 preserves the action without establishing a cause.
The action remains after dental-abscess and dental-fracture reference cards are removed from a test knowledge copy.
negativeExamples: Biting pain alone, injury with biting pain, isolated swelling, or bleeding with swelling does not acquire this new action.
Brief thermal sensitivity, 紧绷 and remote/radiating pain do not satisfy this sufficient trigger.
Restricted opening, swallowing or breathing still retains the existing emergency tier.
notEstablished: These observations do not diagnose an abscess, spreading infection, periodontal disease or acute onset.
The five-label trigger is not an exclusion test: other symptoms can still need dental care.
No validated two-checkbox score, diagnostic performance or guaranteed local access within 24 hours is claimed. No new symptom, condition or anatomy model is added.

entries.type: Anatomical terminology and existing region routing correction

sources.title: Chinese Terms of Human Anatomy, second edition, sections 02.1796 / 02.1687 and 02.1538
sources.use: Distinguishes the foot little-toe opponens from the hand little-finger opponens; locates rotatores between vertebrae. PDF pages 133, 127 and 118 (one based).

sources.title: FIPAT Terminologia Anatomica second edition, Part 2: entries 2284 and 2406
sources.use: Places Rotatores in the back musculature and Pubo-analis in the pelvic diaphragm/levator ani group. Supports anatomical region, not diagnosis or symptom origin.

implementation: Correct the existing foot opponens Chinese label to 小趾对跖肌; retain hand opponens labels and all English/raw mesh names.
Route the exact normalized identities Rotatores and Pubo-analis muscle to existing spine and pelvis regions before broad translated component words can classify them as head or hip.
Keep neighboring cerebral gyri in head, Pectineus in hip, and hand opponens structures in hand. Existing regional symptom filters and safety rules then apply without changing their criteria.
positiveExamples: Both .l/.r foot opponens meshes retain foot with the corrected Chinese term.
Rotatores.l/.r with pain and fever reaches the existing back warning.
Pubo-analis muscle.l/.r with explicit LLQ, pain and fever reaches the existing pelvic/abdominal same-day path.
negativeExamples: Hand opponens labels remain 对掌肌.
Cerebral gyri do not move to spine; Pectineus does not move to pelvis.
Pain alone does not acquire an urgent action merely because the anatomical region was corrected.
limits: The formal Chinese subdivision name for Pubo-analis remains unverified; the later qualified-pubo-analis-display entry uses an explicit parent-level description, not a certified subdivision translation.
The model selection cannot establish the actual symptomatic tissue, disease or geometric laterality. No model, global symptom option or condition ID is added.

entries.type: Presentation-only removal of repeated lower dental actions after an explicitly matched oral emergency

sources.title: NHS Dental abscess: emergency oral symptoms
sources.use: Oral swelling with difficulty swallowing or opening the mouth warrants emergency assessment. This supports prioritizing the matched emergency action; the exact message coverage is an application presentation decision.

implementation: Give the existing oral-swelling/swallowing emergency a stable identity. Preserve every original warning, assessment tier, clinical rule and reference-card action.

Only oral-swelling-dysphagia and oral-swelling-restricted-opening cover the three named lower dental actions, and only when the covering warning has a strictly higher tier. Other warnings remain visible at every level.

A saved canonical reportedSymptoms snapshot supplies a brief bilingual Also reported line for the covered dental observations. It never reads live edited form state or treats reference-card why as a complete history.
positiveExamples: Jaw biting pain, gum swelling and swallowing difficulty show the emergency action plus the actual dental observations, without repeating a lower same-day dental appointment instruction.
Removing the swallowing observation and reassessing restores the complete same-day dental message.
negativeExamples: Facial droop, oral swallowing difficulty and restricted opening retain all three distinct emergency instructions.
A sudden worst headache does not hide an independent biting-pain/fever action.
Unknown warning IDs, unlabelled warnings, unrelated hearing/urinary warnings and equal-tier messages are not covered.
limits: This is a narrow message-coverage policy for the same oral escalation, not a global highest-tier-only filter or a clinical validation.
The additional line is a subset of actual dental observations, not a complete medical history or evidence of absent symptoms.

entries.type: Exact anatomical region correction

sources.title: FIPAT Terminologia Anatomica second edition, Part 2: entries 2655–2669
sources.use: PDF page 76 places Plantaris under the superficial posterior leg compartment, before the separate foot-muscle group.

sources.title: Chinese Terms of Human Anatomy, second edition: 02.1782
sources.use: PDF page 132 describes the small proximal belly and long descending tendon of 跖肌; the whole identity is not a plantar foot muscle.

implementation: Map only normalized plantaris muscle to the existing lower-limb region before generic plantar/跖 word fragments. Retain both languages, raw nodes, left/right identities and all model bytes.
Keep Soleus lower-limb, Calcaneal tendon ankle and Plantar aponeurosis foot. Existing regional controls and rules apply without altering their medical criteria.
positiveExamples: Plantaris muscle.l/.r in both deployed muscle assets route to lower-limb.
Ordinary reported pain produces the broad lower-limb basic reference without assigning a sole or toe location.
negativeExamples: Plantar aponeurosis and other plantar structures are not globally rerouted.
A model selection alone does not establish where along the muscle/tendon discomfort originates.
limits: This corrects the broad anatomical region, not geometric laterality, symptom source or a clinical diagnosis. No option, model or condition is added.

entries.type: Qualified anatomical display terminology

sources.title: FIPAT Terminologia Anatomica second edition, Part 2: entries 2402–2409
sources.use: PDF page 67 places Pubo-analis within the pelvic diaphragm / levator ani subdivision group.

sources.title: Chinese Terms of Human Anatomy, second edition: 03.0905
sources.use: PDF page 193 supports the parent name 肛提肌 for levator ani; it does not certify a direct Chinese translation of the Pubo-analis subdivision used by this atlas.

implementation: Replace the misleading Chinese Pectineus-like subdivision wording with the short parent-level description 肛提肌相关结构.

In Chinese model and panel context, show the curated English subdivision Pubo-analis with a brief explicit provisional-name qualifier. Keep the main name short and retain the existing full English labels, sides and exact pelvis routing.
positiveExamples: Pubo-analis muscle.l/.r keep their actual model identity and side, with a qualified Chinese context.
negativeExamples: Pectineus, the general levator ani and every other structure keep their names and do not acquire the qualifier.
limits: The Chinese phrase is a temporary broad description, not an approved formal subdivision term. TA98/TA2 subdivision synonyms differ; the app does not equate this mesh with another named subdivision or infer the symptom source.

entries.type: Source-informed contact wording; no change to assessment tier or diagnostic gates

sources.title: NHS: Blood in urine
sources.use: Urgent GP/111 contact for seen or suspected blood supports timely triage. This public advice does not establish that every untyped report is visible hematuria or requires hospital emergency assessment.

sources.title: NHS: Jaundice
sources.use: Yellow skin/eyes warrant urgent GP/111 contact. The route is access to clinical triage, not a validated severity score for the app.

sources.title: MSD Professional: Hematuria
sources.use: Visible and microscopic hematuria have different evaluation pathways. Low-risk follow-up depends on history, testing and clinical risk assessment, none of which can be inferred from unselected checkboxes.

sources.title: MSD Professional: Jaundice
sources.use: Associated abdominal symptoms, altered awareness and bleeding affect urgency; history, examination and laboratory findings are needed to assess cause.

sources.title: BSG: Guidelines on the management of abnormal liver blood tests (2017), PDF page 9
sources.use: Immediate referral for unexplained clinical jaundice supports early clinical triage. A self-selected app label does not establish clinically confirmed unexplained jaundice or prescribe the hospital destination.

entries.decision: For isolated blood in urine or jaundice, explicitly advise contacting a medical service today for triage and explaining how/when it was noticed and any prior assessment, diagnosis or follow-up plan. A clinician determines the place and timing of assessment. Keep the existing prompt assessment tier and all existing safety-net clauses and higher-priority predicates unchanged.
entries.appliesTo: The existing single-observation prompt branches, including their coexistence with independent higher-priority warnings. Contact today is a conservative application mapping for unstratified input, not a claim that all patients require a completed hospital assessment today.

positiveExamples.expected: Contact today for triage; prompt tier and basic reference retained.
Contact today for triage; explain onset and prior care without asserting an unexplained new diagnosis.

negativeExamples.expected: Existing immediate action for inability to pass urine remains first.
Dark urine alone is not converted to reported blood.
Pale stool alone is not converted to reported jaundice.

notEstablished: The app does not collect blood visibility/testing subtype, age, full medical history, prior risk assessment or laboratory findings. Unticked warning signs do not establish a low-risk pathway.

No hematuria cancer pathway, jaundice cause, adult/infant identity or deadline for completed investigations is inferred. Existing follow-up plans are information to share with the clinician, not instructions to change treatment.
The sources do not validate the app tiers, scores or diagnostic accuracy. Today contact and same-day clinical assessment are distinct in this wording.
AUA/NICE official search excerpts informed the limitations review only; inaccessible full guideline text was not used to add a rule.

entries.type: Existing observation semantics within reviewed neck/back triage

sources.title: MSD Professional: Overview of Neck and Back Pain, Red flags

entries.decision: The existing night-pain label already reports pain. Within neck/back pathways it satisfies the existing pain component for fever/chills (same-day) and unintentional weight loss (prompt), without requiring another generic pain checkbox. In the existing neck/back basic fallback only, night pain plus reported impact/twisting injury also receives the existing neutral injury wording instead of posture attribution.
positiveExamples: Vertebra L3 and Vertebra C3: 夜间痛 + 发热/发冷
Vertebra L3 and Vertebra C3: 夜间痛 + 体重下降
Vertebra L3 and Vertebra C3: 夜间痛 + 外伤后/扭伤后 gives neutral basic injury guidance
negativeExamples: Night pain alone is not severe night pain and does not automatically raise urgency
Fever alone and pure duration do not acquire a pain fact
Injury alone does not add pain; night pain alone does not add injury
Other areas and remote shoulder pain do not enter this neck/back-specific fallback
notEstablished: No infection or malignancy diagnosis; no added severity, laterality or examination finding.
The change is limited to neck/back triage; PAIN_TAGS, LOCAL_PAIN_TAGS, evidence families and disease gates remain unchanged.

entries.type: Visible-label facts and acute-symptom safety review

sources.title: Merck Professional: Numbness, evaluation and red flags
CDC: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke

entries.decision: The actual elbow-bending label states worsening numbness, and facial numbness explicitly reports a sensory change. Both use the existing broad sensory direction; facial wording asks for actual onset/distribution rather than assuming headache or compression. Explicit facial numbness together with explicit sudden onset receives immediate assessment independent of model side or additional weakness/speech findings.
positiveExamples: Humerus.l: 屈肘加重 alone uses a basic sensory direction; actual ring/little-finger numbness retains the existing ulnar reference gate
Frontal bone, Mandible and Incus.l: 面部麻木 alone uses a basic sensory direction; adding 突然起病 gives emergency guidance
negativeExamples: Facial numbness alone or with recurring-for-months does not establish sudden onset
Elbow-provoked numbness alone or with sudden onset does not satisfy the facial-specific trigger
notEstablished: The model side does not prove symptom laterality. No stroke, palsy, peripheral entrapment or nerve distribution is diagnosed from these choices.
Sudden facial numbness is an observed warning combination, not a validated scoring rule. Unknown onset is not evidence of chronic or benign symptoms.

entries.type: Locality of reported evidence and qualified reference copy

sources.title: Merck Professional: Bursitis, symptoms and diagnosis

entries.decision: The shoulder-specific side-lying pain label can support the shoulder bursitis reference only. It cannot supply hip/knee/ankle local evidence or a missing local-evidence suggestion. Actual local tenderness remains usable. The reference description presents possible features and requests examination rather than asserting unreported tenderness. Non-shoulder basic cards also exclude that remote observation from local evidence and retain an explicit shoulder-context note; a lone shoulder observation uses neutral actual-site clarification, while independent fatigue, skin or urinary directions remain available.
positiveExamples: Scapula.l: 局部肿胀 + 侧卧肩痛 retains the existing reference
Patella.l, Talus.r and Pectineus muscle.r: 局部肿胀 + 局部压痛 retains the existing reference
negativeExamples: Patella.l, Talus.r and Pectineus muscle.r: 局部肿胀 + 侧卧肩痛 does not establish bursitis at the selected site
notEstablished: No new condition or observation ID; visibility lists remain unchanged. The original shoulder observation remains in reportedSymptoms.
Other existing kneeling/location pathways are preserved, not newly clinically validated by this review.

entries.type: Existing regional safety predicates consuming an explicit pain observation

sources.title: NHS: Ectopic pregnancy, symptoms and medical advice

entries.decision: The existing night pain label reports pain without severity or new quality. Within the reviewed chest, abdominal/pelvic and confirmed-flank safety branches only, it satisfies the original pain premise. Every original location, associated sign, onset and persistence condition is preserved. The prior disposition source entries remain applicable; this is not a new night-pain risk standard.
positiveExamples: Body of sternum and Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle.r: night pain with breathlessness or cold sweat
Rectus abdominis muscle.r / Levator ani.or: night pain plus possible pregnancy, with or without a known quadrant
Explicit LLQ/RLQ/flank and the original upper-abdominal combinations with night pain
negativeExamples: Night pain alone, or sudden onset without the separately required persistence, is not automatically an emergency
Duration alone does not report pain; unknown/diffuse location cannot supply a specific quadrant
Epigastric night pain with cold sweat does not imply the dedicated pressure symptom
notEstablished: No pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, cardiac disease, infection, stone, organ injury or other diagnosis is established by these selections.
No general pain token is inserted, no global PAIN/LOCAL/REPORTED set or evidence family is changed, and no condition gate is loosened.
The generic Sternum/Pectoralis major aliases were replaced by verified visible mesh names in final cases. Full/mobile identity and per-field availability are tested; this is not clinical validation.
existingCoreBranches: chest pain with danger signs or explicitly sudden and persistent onset
explicit flank pain with systemic fever/chills
continuingLimits: Night pain remains outside unreviewed pain predicates; this entry does not certify all clinical warning coverage.

entries.type: Existing head safety predicates consuming an explicit pain observation

sources.title: MSD Professional: Approach to the Patient With Headache, history and red flags
sources.use: Pain timing is distinct from severity and onset. Fever, progressive worsening and neurological findings such as diplopia or weakness warrant assessment.

sources.title: NHS: Double vision
sources.use: Distinguishes urgent sudden diplopia from immediate advice for severe headache with diplopia. Night pain alone does not establish the severe-headache premise.

sources.title: American Stroke Association: Stroke Symptoms
sources.use: Sudden visual changes, including double vision, are neurological warning signs requiring prompt emergency action. This does not diagnose stroke.

entries.decision: Within the three previously reviewed head-pain clauses only, the night pain observation satisfies the existing reported-pain premise. Fever/chills/progression and diplopia/reduced strength retain their existing same-day actions; explicit sudden onset with head pain and diplopia retains the existing conservative emergency action. The separate sudden-motor-loss clause is unchanged.
positiveExamples: Frontal bone: night pain plus fever, chills or progressive worsening
Frontal bone: night pain plus diplopia or reduced strength
Frontal bone: night pain plus explicit sudden onset and diplopia
negativeExamples: Night pain alone or night pain with sudden onset alone does not automatically escalate.
Fever, worsening or duration alone does not establish head pain.
Isolated diplopia, sudden diplopia without pain, isolated weakness and sudden weakness retain their previous actions.
Humerus.l night pain with fever is outside this head-only extension; independent sudden facial numbness remains an emergency.
notEstablished: Night pain does not establish severe pain, thunderclap onset, nocturnal awakening, symptom laterality, stroke, meningitis, tumour or an imaging indication.

NHS immediate advice requires severe headache, which the night-pain label does not report. The explicit sudden-head-pain/visual-change emergency mapping remains the previously reviewed conservative application policy, not a validated night-pain score.
Sources use different urgency wording for isolated diplopia; that separate policy is not changed in this batch.
No general pain tag is inserted, no global pain set or evidence family changes, and no condition P gate is widened. Night pain remains spontaneous in the existing evidence taxonomy.

All source fixtures use visible full/mobile GLB identities and field-visible labels. Generic pain is not available in the head UI; the software equivalence comparison uses the existing selectable stinging label. Synthetic software checks are not clinical validation.

entries.type: Existing exercise/urine safety predicate consuming an explicit pain observation

sources.title: MSD Professional: Rhabdomyolysis
sources.use: Exercise-related pain, weakness and dark urine can require urgent assessment. The complete triad is uncommon; symptoms alone neither establish nor exclude the diagnosis.

sources.title: CDC/NIOSH: Signs and Symptoms of Rhabdomyolysis
sources.use: Describes pain, dark urine and weakness, possible delayed appearance, and the need for immediate medical care and testing.

entries.decision: Night pain supplies only the original reported-pain premise in exercise-muscle-urine-warning. The musculoskeletal region list, exercise or delayed exercise-soreness observation, dark urine, and at least one of weakness/swelling/progression are all retained. The original conservative emergency action is reused without a model-tissue restriction.
positiveExamples: Humerus.l: night pain + exercise/extra load + dark urine + reduced strength, local swelling or progressive worsening
Rectus femoris muscle.r: the same complete observation combination
negativeExamples: Missing exercise, dark urine or the final accompanying-signal group does not activate this predicate.
Night pain alone and dark urine alone do not automatically escalate.
The existing delayed exercise-soreness route retains its original action.
notEstablished: Dark urine is not proven myoglobinuria; reported reduced strength is not an objective examination. No rhabdomyolysis diagnosis, severity, injury mechanism or laboratory result is invented.
Negative test cases mean this sufficient software trigger is unmet, not that disease is excluded or dehydration is safe to assume.
No general pain tag is inserted; global pain sets, disease P gates and evidence families remain unchanged.

entries.type: Existing eye-injury review predicate consuming an explicit pain observation

sources.title: NHS: Eye injuries
sources.use: Separates post-injury assessment from immediate actions for severe pain, visual changes, photophobia or high-risk mechanisms. Night timing does not establish these additional findings.

entries.decision: For the original eye region plus reported injury review only, night pain satisfies the original discomfort/pain premise without requiring an extra stinging checkbox. The existing same-day review is retained; all separately reported higher-priority eye findings keep their previous emergency actions.
positiveExamples: Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi.l: night pain + reported injury, with or without an additional stinging observation
negativeExamples: Night pain alone, injury alone or injury plus duration alone does not add the eye-injury review.
A non-eye selection does not receive this eye-specific review from the change.
notEstablished: Night pain does not establish severe pain, symptoms lasting 24 hours, a penetrating injury, a confirmed globe injury or a diagnosis. Selecting an eyelid muscle does not identify the injured tissue.
Without a selected pain observation is not a history of explicitly absent pain.
No global reported-pain function, disease gate, visible option, anatomy asset or existing high-priority eye rule is changed.

entries.type: Bilingual observation-label consistency

sources.title: American Stroke Association: Stroke Symptoms, B.E. F.A.S.T. speech
sources.use: A new speech warning warrants immediate help; uncertainty about the exact onset is not an exclusion criterion.

sources.title: CDC: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
sources.use: Speech difficulty is a stroke warning; note onset and seek immediate help rather than waiting to establish every detail.

entries.decision: Change only the Chinese label for the existing 说话含糊 ID to 新出现说话含糊, matching New slurred speech. Keep the existing emergency action, predicate and warning text. New describes a change from the prior state and does not automatically establish sudden onset.
entries.appliesTo: The existing selectable speech observation. Frontal bone provides a verified two-asset UI path; a separate sudden-onset checkbox remains optional for this existing action.
notEstablished: This is not a diagnosis of stroke, an examination of speech, or confirmation of an objective onset time.
Known longstanding stable or clearly chronic progressive speech changes are not separately characterized by this input and were not newly validated.
NICE full guidance was not retrieved in this review and is not cited as full-text support.

entries.type: Bilingual observation-label consistency

sources.title: American Association of Endodontists: Endodontic Diagnosis, pages 2–3
sources.use: Distinguishes pain settling after a thermal stimulus is removed from pain that persists after removal; symptom descriptions alone do not establish the tissue diagnosis.

entries.decision: For the existing 刺激去除即缓解 ID, retain 冷热刺激一停就好 and replace Brief sensitivity with Pain stops when hot/cold stimulus ends. Preserve its existing combination with thermal sensitivity and the lingering-pain exclusion.
entries.appliesTo: The existing dental observation and its displayed matched detail, verified on Lower canine.l in both shipped model qualities.
notEstablished: Brief duration alone does not supply the stimulus-removal relationship.
No new seconds cutoff, symptom, diagnostic criterion or treatment indication is introduced.
Relief after stimulus removal alone cannot distinguish dentin sensitivity from reversible pulp irritation.

entries.type: Bilingual reference safety-net consistency

sources.title: MSD Manual Professional: Acute Bacterial Meningitis
sources.use: Fever, headache and neck stiffness can indicate an urgent evaluation context; requiring a high fever is not supported as an exclusion boundary.

sources.title: NHS: Meningitis
sources.use: Supports urgent assessment of concerning combinations without assuming every possible symptom must be present.

entries.decision: In the head-pressure-pattern reference threshold only, change 伴高热颈硬 to 伴发热和颈部僵硬. Retain fever with stiff neck in English, the AND relationship and the existing emergency instruction.
entries.appliesTo: A conditional future safety net on an existing reference card. Frontal bone with band-like pressure and bilateral headache displays the card without a priority override.
notEstablished: The selected headache observations do not establish that fever or neck stiffness is currently present.
This does not diagnose meningitis, add a temperature cutoff or a new neck-stiffness input, or modify an independent triage predicate.
Absent or unreported high fever cannot be used to exclude infection.

entries.type: Source-reviewed supportive advice wording

sources.title: NHS: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), Treatment
sources.use: Urinary symptoms should be assessed; a clinician may perform a urine test, but it is not always needed. The page distinguishes care pathways by age, pregnancy and other clinical circumstances.

entries.decision: In urinary-tract-infection-pattern advice only, retain prompt assessment in both languages and clarify that a clinician decides whether urine testing is needed. Keep the existing ordinary appropriate hydration wording. No reference gate, priority predicate, level or warning text changes.
entries.appliesTo: The existing urinary reference without a priority override. Actual Anterior longitudinal ligament reports with painful urination and urinary frequency or urgency display this advice. Existing fever, blood-in-urine and retention priorities still replace reference advice.
notEstablished: A model location or reference match does not establish infection, patient age, pregnancy, reproductive anatomy, catheter use or medical history.
This does not tell users that testing is unnecessary; population-specific assessment and testing remain clinical decisions.
The original prompt contact intent is retained, without a new same-day rule, test prescription, medicine or fluid-volume target.
NICE NG109 recommendations were available only as official search excerpts during the source review; the full page returned 403 and was not treated as a directly read source.

entries.type: Source-reviewed clinical action-place wording calibration

sources.title: NHS: Appendicitis, urgent and immediate advice
sources.use: Worsening or migrating right-lower abdominal pain warrants urgent medical assessment; severe abdominal pain or sepsis-like findings require immediate emergency help. Assessment can start through an urgent primary-care/triage service and may require hospital tests and treatment.

entries.decision: Keep the existing same-day predicate and priority order. Replace the blanket Chinese emergency-department location instruction with explicit urgent medical assessment the same day, and make the same-day timing explicit in English. Fever remains an optional concerning accompaniment, not a required prerequisite.
entries.appliesTo: The existing migrating-right-lower-pain or confirmed RLQ pain-plus-worsening warning across its current abdominal/pelvic entries. All warning predicates, severity levels, identifiers and independent emergency overrides are unchanged.
notEstablished: This is a clinically meaningful adjustment of the place-of-care wording, not merely a translation correction or evidence of diagnostic validity.
Progressively worsening pain does not establish severe or sudden severe pain, and model anatomy does not establish appendicitis.
The UK urgent GP/111 pathway is not a guarantee that outpatient care is sufficient or that emergency care is inappropriate; hospital evaluation may still be needed.
Retaining same-day urgent assessment does not permit watchful waiting or a routine appointment delay.

entries.type: Source-reviewed clinical action-place and reported-fact wording calibration

sources.title: SANJO: diagnostic approach, recommendations 1 and 3
sources.use: Possible native-joint infection needs prompt clinical assessment and, when suspected, aspiration as soon as possible. Clinical observations alone do not confirm or exclude infection.

sources.title: NHS: Septic arthritis, when and where to get help
sources.use: Suspected infection warrants urgent medical help; an urgent GP/111 assessment is an initial route, while confirmed infection usually requires hospital treatment.

entries.decision: Keep the existing same-day swelling-plus-systemic-fever/chills predicate and urgent assessment today. Describe the reported swelling and fever or feeling cold/chills, with the actual joint or surrounding tissue involvement left for examination; selecting a whole humerus does not establish joint involvement.
entries.appliesTo: Only the bilingual text of the existing main-engine swelling with fever/chills warning. The separate hot-swollen-joint literature rule, reference gates, body-region list and all independent emergency priorities are unchanged.
notEstablished: This changes a clinically meaningful care-location instruction and avoids an unestablished anatomical assertion; it is not clinical validation.
SANJO concerns clinician-assessed possible or confirmed native-joint infection and does not turn these checkboxes into a diagnosis or specify the only initial care setting for every user.
Urgent assessment today is retained as a conservative application policy. It does not promise that a clinic is sufficient or exclude emergency referral or admission.
The existing 发冷 / 寒战 input is not upgraded to confirmed rigors. Model side is not confirmed symptom side.
Missing either trigger is not evidence excluding infection, and treatment-timing guidance for already assessed patients must not justify delaying an initial assessment.

retainedBoundaries.reason: Age, full episode frequency/duration, treatment response, objective neurological/joint/eye/hearing examination, laboratories and imaging are not collected. Do not claim complete ICHD, Ottawa imaging, stone obstruction or organ diagnosis.
Unticked symptoms are unknown. Cannot infer no fever/infection, no pregnancy, no neurological finding, stable bleeding, confirmed side or absence of serious disease.

No hearing subtype, monocular/binocular diplopia, eye versus periocular pus origin, bleed volume, continuous active bleeding or completed pressure trial is known. Preserve explicit conditional safety-net instructions.
Checkbox weakness is not an examination. The actual weight-loss label reports unintentional loss, but does not establish a cause. Model anatomy cannot prove the symptomatic tissue or source.

Do not add hard diagnostic gates from inaccessible complete sources, historical disease mechanisms, conflicting rest/activity advice, or superficial resemblance. No new medication, imaging decision or diagnosis model was introduced.

Pin-prick and stinging words are not established as interchangeable in every condition. They share a general pain evidence family, but no unsupported blanket synonym substitution was added. Exact duplication and ordering are stable.
The existing autonomic-assessment condition has no selectable structure in the current three layers. It remains explicitly unavailable; no model was added to make a test pass.
Public-source review and synthetic software tests cannot estimate diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity or patient safety. No patient dataset or clinician validation is claimed.
